paper_metadata.title: Effect of Hf on high-temperature strength and room-temperature ductility of Nb–15W–0.5Si–2B alloy

evidence.quote: Mechanical responses of Nb–15W–0.5Si–2B– xHf alloys ( x = 0, 5, 10 and 15 mol%) were investigated to probe the balance between room-temperature ductility and high-temperature strength depending on Hf concentration in Nb-based solid solution.

The microstructure of Nb–15W–0.5Si–2B–(0–15)Hf alloy is composed of two phases. The overwhelming phase is the Nb solid-solution, NbSS, and the minority grey phase is the Nb–B boride with a volume fraction less than 5%.

because Hf and Ti have the same crystal structure (hcp) and both of them show the same propensity towards ductilization of the NbSS, the ductilization of the Nb SS by Hf may also be dominated by either one of the unstable stacking energy and the Peierls–Nabarro barrier energy or both.

With a Nb solid-solution dominant microstructure, the Nb–15W–0.5Si–2B–15Hf alloy shows a 0.2% compressive yield strength of as high as 365 MPa even at 1400 ◦C, while its compressive ductility at room temperature is about 17%.
